correctness.rationale: The cut encoding and trace quantifiers are exact. Private sites are necessary from single-negative patterns, \(\tau\le c\) from all-negative, complement size at least \(c\) from all-positive. A proved interval no-triple-overlap lemma allows a minimum hitting set for any prescribed negative subfamily to be moved onto private sites without creating forbidden hits, then padded outside all support intervals to exactly c cuts. Upper bounds use disjoint private sites, up to two support intervals per cut site, and reservation of c unused sites. Three-site paired overlap gadgets and isolated singleton intervals attain the simultaneous bound in every parameter regime. A separate brute-force trace generator compared 397284 support cases, 45 exact VC dimension cases and 3040 deterministic additional support cases. The infinite statement is proved, not extrapolated from those tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Refinement-closed theorems apply to unions of all finer partitions, not exactly c+1 blocks. The fixed-size bipartition forest theorem constrains the cardinality of one side and allows nonconsecutive blocks. The interval-union VC result uses a different primal incidence domain and at-most-k intervals. None covers the precise fixed-cardinality dual interval-hitting concept on a finite line, including its floor(m/2) and m-c corrections.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The unrestricted private-site criterion is necessary but not sufficient at fixed c, because all-negative patterns require tau<=c and all-positive patterns require at least c completely unused cut sites. The current theorem derives those conditions and uses a no-triple-overlap lemma to prove sufficiency; its sharp dimension min(2c,floor(m/2),m-c) is strictly below the unrestricted m for m>=2 and is not a corollary of an unrestricted dimension assertion. Neither refinement closure nor arbitrary-size two-block partitions can be substituted for a fixed exact number of convex blocks.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A fixed set of c cut sites corresponds to exactly c+1 contiguous equivalence blocks. Equivalently, this is the rank-c slice of the Boolean lattice acting on all nonempty intervals by intersection; pair-equality is its complementary incidence. The unrestricted equivalence family allows every rank and shatters a support iff each interval has a private site, but rank-c adds the compulsory at-most-c piercing and at-least-c outside-union tests. Full inspected statements do not include these fixed-rank requirements.

value.rationale: The exact number of convex equivalence classes is a motivated model-complexity constraint in segmentation and ordered clustering. This is a full all-parameter support criterion with three simultaneous resource constraints, a sharp nonmonotone \(\min\{2c,\lfloor m/2\rfloor,m-c\}\) dimension law, and explicit witnesses. This cannot be deduced as a routine count from unrestricted convex partitions, where the dimension is m, and it gives information not provided by scalar learning bounds or unrelated partitions.
